title: Urologist visit
what: The doctor asks about your symptoms, examines your urinary and genital organs, and orders tests or an ultrasound if needed.
why: For frequent or painful urination, blood in the urine, pain in the lower back or groin, or erection problems. For men over 45 to 50, as a checkup.
tell_doctor: What medicines you take, especially blood thinners
If you have had stones, surgery, or infections
How often you pass urine during the day and at night
Your PSA results, if you have had the test

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: A normal shower the evening before or in the morning.

prepare.title: Bladder
prepare.text: If you will have a bladder ultrasound or a urine test, come with a moderately full bladder. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: PSA test
prepare.text: If you need a PSA test, blood is usually taken before the prostate exam. For 2 days before the test, avoid ejaculation and cycling.

bring: Recent urine and blood tests, and PSA
Ultrasound reports and past medical records
steps: The doctor asks about your symptoms
The doctor looks at and feels your belly, lower back, and outer genitals
In men, the prostate is usually checked with a finger through the back passage
Women are examined on an exam chair, much like a gynecology exam
Sometimes an ultrasound is done right away
The doctor explains which tests and exams you need
feel: The prostate exam is an unpleasant pressure for a few seconds, but usually not painful
You may feel the urge to pass urine. This is normal
Slow, calm breathing helps you relax
after: You can go back to your day straight away
Test results are usually ready in 1 to 3 days
red_flags: You cannot pass urine and your belly feels very full
Fever with chills and pain in the lower back
Blood and clots in the urine
Sudden severe pain in a testicle: call emergency services right away. Every hour counts

faq.a: Usually not. It is an unpleasant pressure for a few seconds. The exam is simple but very useful.

faq.q: Should I see a urologist if nothing hurts?
faq.a: Men over 45 to 50 are usually advised to have a checkup once a year. Many prostate problems cause no symptoms for a long time.
